title: Order wagon appendix headings by the documented heading order

facts.note: Scope is any wagon document that has, or is gaining, appendix sections; identifiable by path and file kind. Applies to any agent editing such a document, not only the planner.

Fires on writing or modifying ANY part of a wagon document that has or gains appendix sections, including body edits unrelated to the appendices. The structural invariant is re-checked over the whole document on every such edit.

values: appendix section added, removed or edited
appendix heading added, renamed or reordered
main-body heading or anchor targeted by appendix back-links renamed, moved or removed
facts.note: NON-EXCLUSIVE optimization only: a diff-level observer may use these change types to prioritise or focus the check, but must not gate activation on them. Any edit of a wagon document with appendices activates the rule even if none of these change types is present.

fires: An appendix section is added to a wagon document.
Appendix headings in an existing wagon document are reordered or renamed.
A new wagon document is written that contains supplementary sections.
A main-body heading or anchor that existing appendix back-links point to is renamed, moved or removed.
An unrelated main-body paragraph is edited in a wagon document that already has appendix sections (the whole document's appendix structure is re-checked).
doesNotFire: Source code, tests or acceptance files that are not wagon documents.
Documents that are not wagon documents (e.g. unrelated READMEs or other plan documents).
Wagon documents that have no appendix sections and are not gaining any.

given: A wagon document has, or is gaining, appendix sections (supplementary sections of the wagon document).
when: Any part of that wagon document is authored or edited — appendix sections, main-body headings/anchors, or unrelated body content.
then: The appendix headings follow the documented heading order.
prefer: Take the heading sequence from the documented heading order for wagon appendices rather than inventing one per document; if that documentation cannot be located, report the gap instead of choosing an order.
Keep the companion obligation (see split suggestion): every appendix section links back to the main wagon body — write each back-link as you write the section.
After any edit to the document, especially renaming or moving a main-body heading, re-check that every appendix back-link still resolves.
avoid: Appendix headings in ad-hoc or per-author order.
Any appendix section without a working link back to the main wagon body (orphaned supplementary content, or a back-link broken by a main-body edit).
why: A fixed appendix heading order and back-links keep large wagon documents navigable and auditable.
evidence: Reviewer compares the appendix headings in the wagon document against the documented heading order and finds them in sequence.
Reviewer confirms every appendix section contains a link back to the main wagon body that resolves to an existing main-body target; a missing or broken back-link is a finding (companion obligation).
verifier_detail: Term appendix_section: a supplementary section of a wagon document.
Term heading_order: the documented sequence the appendix headings must follow.
Severity 1; disposition documentation-only (guidance for documents, not an enforced code gate).

Two independently checkable mandatory requirements from the single source statement: (a) appendix headings match the documented heading order; (b) each appendix section has a back-link to the main wagon body. Failing either is a separate finding. Check both over the whole document on every edit of a wagon document with appendices, regardless of which part was edited.
Naming, storage and taxonomy of appendices are decomposed into planner.appendix.naming-pattern, planner.appendix.storage and planner.appendix.types (graph edges).
audit: Original statement: Appendix sections follow the documented heading order and link back to the main wagon body.

splitSuggestion.then: Every appendix section of a wagon document links back to the main wagon body, and that link resolves to an existing main-body target.

additions.text: The source statement holds two independently violable obligations: heading order (kept as then) and per-section back-links (proposed as planner.appendix.back-links). Until split, the back-link requirement stays mandatory here via prefer[1], avoid[1], evidence[1] and verifier_detail[3].
additions.justification: One-obligation rule; auditor required both requirements to be independently checkable without losing either.

additions.text: Activation covers any authoring or edit of a wagon document with appendices, including unrelated body edits; the change fact is a non-exclusive optimization, never a gate. No actor restriction.
additions.justification: Auditor: source states an unconditional structural invariant; activation must not be narrowed to selected change types.

additions.text: If the documented heading order cannot be located, report the gap instead of choosing an order; re-check back-links after edits, especially main-body heading changes; write back-links while authoring each section.
additions.justification: Concrete moves that satisfy the source obligations; add no new obligation.

additions.text: Reviewer checks of heading order and of resolving back-links.
additions.justification: Source has no evidence section; these are the direct verification of the statement.

trace.note: Heading order is then; back-link obligation kept mandatory via prefer[1]/avoid[1]/evidence[1]/verifier_detail[3] and proposed as split planner.appendix.back-links.
